prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: complete map composition for one real Snabbit level, "Three Switches, One Door".
Primary request: Suggest a beautiful authored puzzle map in the original game art: three chunky orange levers toggle the SAME final stone door. The first and last levers sit in unavoidable one-cell throats. The middle lever sits on a genuinely optional left branch around a central pointed stone sail, with a clear right bypass. Taking all three toggles leaves the one final gate open; bypassing the middle produces two toggles and closes the door.
Scene/backdrop: deep plain navy space, original faceted silver asteroid sprites, sparse cyan gems and exactly three yellow star collectibles.
Style/medium: crisp 2D original game sprite map, top-down flat orthographic, individual separate chunky asteroid cells on the game's staggered offset-hex grid. References are genuine first-three-level contact sheets for all three prior packs, actual source sprites including the chunky lever, and an accepted introductory level. Preserve that art style, do not invent textures or new game elements.
Composition/framing: one tall portrait map, about 16 columns by 52 rows. Bottom is entrance and top is finish. Sculpt a single asymmetric hollow asteroid lantern: a thick chipped left crescent, a shorter lumpy right wing, a central pointed sail splitting the middle into two unequal branching hollows, and a small upper exit bowl. Lower and upper compulsory lever throats should feel like natural pinches between rocky shoulders, not full-width wall strips. Middle optional lever sits in the generous left hollow beside the sail, reachable without damage; right branch is empty and reconnects before the upper compulsory lever. Three levers total, visually identical. A single short 2-cell stone gate sits six rows above the upper compulsory lever. Keep it plain original silver stone, no color code. A star lies between first and middle levers, another after the last compulsory lever, final star inside exit bowl behind the final gate. Short local gold-sparkle finish at top. Optional middle branch, upper compulsory lever and final door should be close enough to be seen together before committing.
Lighting/mood: quietly inviting but intriguing, high readability, generous dark breathing space inside the hollows and around silhouette.
Constraints: use original silver asteroid, dark rock, gold star, cyan gem and grey/orange chunky lever sprite language. All paths climb upward diagonally left/right, no backward routes, no loops that require descending. No UI, labels, letters, arrows, route overlay, debug colored wall markers, numbers or text.
Avoid: three repeated identical rooms, repeated horizontal strips, obvious constant zigzag, straight gem rails, three unrelated gates, machinery, painterly scenery, symmetry, ultra-narrow long corridors, continuous floor/path tiles. Make this a memorable sculptural silhouette rather than a diagram.
